title: The Man of God from Judah
lead: An unnamed prophet from Judah who condemned Jeroboam's altar at Bethel and named Josiah three centuries ahead, then was deceived by an old prophet of Bethel, disobeyed God's command and was killed by a lion (1 Kings 13). Josiah later spared his grave (2 Kings 23:17–18).

sections.b: By the LORD's word the man of God cries against the altar at Bethel, gives a sign that comes true, heals Jeroboam's stiffened hand, and refuses to eat or drink in Bethel (1 Kings 13:1–10). An old prophet deceives him with a claim that an angel has spoken, then receives a true word that he will not be buried with his ancestors; a lion kills him on the road (1 Kings 13:11–25). The old prophet buries him and asks to be laid beside him (1 Kings 13:26–32). When Josiah defiles the altar with bones from the nearby graves, he spares this grave and with it the old prophet's bones (2 Kings 23:15–18). Josephus calls the man of God Jadon (Antiquities 8.231). Karl Barth gave the chapter a famous theological reading as a parable of election and rejection.
